capabilities.verb: Summon your assistant with a hotkey from anywhere
capabilities.summary: A global hotkey opens a few-pixel launcher over your work; answers stream in place, and Ctrl+D hands the turn to the full desktop window.
proofs: Default hotkey Control+Space, configurable in Settings
The launcher grows without flicker, keeps streaming status on one line, and highlights Expand on overflow
Ctrl+D hands a running turn to the desktop window; expanded mode opens at the start of the latest reply
Replies reveal in paced words with a gentle fade and the same wrapping they keep when finished
Attachments take PDFs, images and live screen captures

capabilities.verb: Choose your update channel and check from Settings
capabilities.summary: Settings → About offers stable and beta channels plus a manual check against the family version API — metadata only, no identifiers ever leave the app, and nothing installs without your explicit consent.
proofs: Stable and beta channels switchable in Settings → About
Manual check with the result and the release page shown inline
The check is a plain GET — no install ID, no usage reporting, ever
AppImage installs in place after two explicit clicks (download, then restart-to-update)
Windows/macOS/deb: the checksum-verified official installer opens with a few wizard clicks

capabilities.verb: Act on your computer only with your approval
capabilities.summary: A risk-classed tool agent (screen capture, shell, files, apps, web) pauses on an approval card whenever your verification preset asks; destructive tools confirm every time.
proofs: Every tool declares read-only, state-changing or destructive
Destructive tools confirm every single time; no setting bypasses it
Unanswered approval requests auto-deny after 60 seconds
File and shell tools stay inside folders you grant via the OS picker
Every tool call is audited locally with outcome, duration and approver

capabilities.verb: Keep every conversation on your machine
capabilities.summary: History, memory, audit logs and settings live in one local SQLite database; provider keys stay in your OS keyring — no accounts, no telemetry.
proofs: One local SQLite database holds history, audits and agent checkpoints
Provider, STT and MCP secrets live in the OS keyring, never in config files
No accounts, no user tables, no telemetry — the OS user is the identity
History, memory and audit logs never leave the machine

capabilities.verb: Bring your own model — cloud or fully local
capabilities.summary: A setup wizard connects OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter or local Ollama — plus a decision-model card — and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works by hand.
proofs: First-run wizard validates the key against the vendor and binds default models
Local Ollama is detected automatically when it is running
Every task slot — vision, transcription, speech, embeddings — gets its own model
Per-conversation model override and persona in the desktop inspector
A Custom / manual card covers any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint

capabilities.verb: Connect your own tools and smart home over MCP
capabilities.summary: Model Context Protocol servers join the agent over stdio, streamable HTTP or SSE, under the same approval gates and audit as native tools.
proofs: MCP tools run under the same approval gates as native tools
The Home Assistant preset pre-configures endpoint, tool risk, entity scope and grounding
Per-server and per-tool kill switches, allowlists and health checks
Server secrets live in the OS keyring, never in config files
MCP results are treated as observations, never as instructions

capabilities.verb: Ask your assistant about your calendar — and let it book
capabilities.summary: Bind Google or Microsoft 365 with your own desktop OAuth client and control the calendar from chat: what's on Thursday, move my 3pm, add an exam. Writes always ask first.
proofs: One-time setup: Settings → Calendar names the environment variable, copies it and links the setup guide
calendar_list and calendar_search are read-only
calendar_create and calendar_move need your approval each time
No delete tool — nothing is ever removed without you
Scopes and destinations are shown verbatim before you consent; tokens stay in the OS keyring

capabilities.verb: Connect reviewed services in one step
capabilities.summary: Bundled presets for Home Assistant, GitHub, Slack, Notion and more pre-fill the endpoint, auth target, tool risk and scoping — you add only the token.
proofs: 18 reviewed presets ship with the app; any custom MCP server connects the same way
Each preset carries authored tool risk, keyword tags and usage guidance
Per-app scope rules check every entity argument against allow/deny globs
Risk overrides are tighten-only: a tool can be made stricter, never looser
Test connection reports latency and tool count; health chips update live

capabilities.verb: Automate prompts on a schedule or a hotkey
capabilities.summary: Scheduled prompts and mini-app runs fire on interval, daily, weekday or cron rhythms in your timezone, and any custom command can bind to a global hotkey.
proofs: Rhythms: every N minutes, daily, weekdays or 5-field cron, in your timezone
Scheduling is DST-safe across fall-back and spring-forward hours
Command hotkeys run a bound command as a normal turn, approvals intact
Scheduled mini-app runs are report-only and never arm anything

capabilities.verb: Dictate input and hear replies spoken aloud
capabilities.summary: Dictate through the transcription model you assign, with fail-closed auto-send, and hear replies read aloud through your assigned speech model.
proofs: Push-to-talk: hold Control in the launcher, release to transcribe
Voice auto-send is fail-closed: an unfinished phrase keeps listening
Interim transcript appears per phrase; transcription language can be pinned
Choose a preset voice for the assigned speech model or type a custom name, with a preview
Custom names reach the provider unchanged; keyless localhost servers need no dummy key

capabilities.verb: Select text anywhere and have it read aloud
capabilities.summary: One hotkey reads your selection aloud through the speech model: a HUD with pause/resume, a content-addressed audio cache so repeats are instant, and an honest clipboard fallback where selection cannot be read.
proofs: Global hotkey (default Ctrl+Shift+S, editable) speaks the current selection without opening the launcher
Speaking HUD with pause/resume and stop — the same state as the launcher bar, tray and hotkeys; it hides while the launcher is open
Repeated selections and replays are served from the audio cache with no new synthesis call
Cache off, a full disk or read-only data still speak — playback never depends on the cache
Wayland without wl-clipboard says the selection is not readable instead of pretending nothing was selected; Speak clipboard is the fallback

capabilities.verb: Keep speech and everyday actions on one edge hub
capabilities.summary: The edge dock is the full hub with mode-aware controls; the dot orb opens a hover strip of Speak/Dictate/Live glass buttons with its own ordering; the now-playing card shows only while speech or live is active.
proofs: Dock states show Quick actions plus speech Pause/Stop, dictation Send/Stop or live Interrupt/End; response hover Copy
The dot orb's hover strip offers Speak selection, Dictate and Live toggle in a user-set order; dictation keeps Send/Stop open on the orb
The card fades when idle even when pinned, and mini bar selections migrate to the dot
Translation results stay in the panel with copy/open/retry; clicking the dock line opens the launcher with the text selected
HUD size presets resize the 204–240 px face, 22–26 px square glass controls and 11–13 px text; Custom applies once

capabilities.verb: Extend it with your own mini-app packs
capabilities.summary: Author or import sandboxed mini-app packs that run inside the assistant: validated manifests, declared capabilities, quarantine with restore.
proofs: Imported packs are validated field-by-field; invalid ones install nothing
Packs run in a sandboxed utility process with only their declared capabilities
The bundled Deletion review moves candidates to quarantine and restores any of them
Author packs with the bundled SDK, validator and pack CLI

useCases: Ask mid-task without breaking flow — press Control+Space, drop in a screenshot, and read the streaming answer in a launcher that grows only as needed.
Delegate a cleanup safely — run a Deletion review over a downloads folder; risky verdicts stop on approval cards and restores are one click.
Run the smart home by sentence — “dim the living room” dispatches through the Home Assistant preset with entity scope enforced.
Automate a weekly report-only pass — schedule a mini-app run on a cron rhythm in your timezone; it produces a report and can never arm anything.
Work offline — point the assistant at local Ollama, dictate by push-to-talk, and search indexed local documents with no provider configured.
